substantial.problem: 'In 1715 the first permanent Russian mission came to Peking' overstates the source. Adoratskii's '1715' (line 550-551, 'Мысль о постоянной миссии въ Пекинѣ осуществилась въ 1715 г.') is the year the plan was carried out; on arrival he is explicitly uncertain: the mission left Tobolsk on 3 February 1715 and 'reached Peking at the end of 1715 or the beginning of 1716'. A date the source gives as uncertain is stated as settled.
substantial.evidence: Library file adoratskii...vyp1, lines 3797-3803 (OCR '1115' for 1715). Page image archive.org pravoslavnajamissijavkitaeza200leteesusc7 page/n73 (printed p. 68), read directly: 'выѣхали изъ Тобольска 3 февраля 1715 г. ... Въ Пекинъ они прибыли къ концу 1715 или въ началѣ 1716 года'. p. 9 (n14) confirms 'осуществилась въ 1715 г.' cleanly.
substantial.fix: Replace the sentence with two: "The first permanent Russian mission set out with the emperor's leave in 1715. It reached Peking at the end of that year or early in 1716." Add a fact_table row: file adoratskii...vyp1, lines 3802-3803, quote 'Въ Пекинъ они прибыли къ концу 1115 или въ на- чалЪ 1716 года' (OCR '1115'; page image reads 1715), rendering 'They arrived in Peking at the end of 1715 or the beginning of 1716'. Whole paragraph as revised (with ASA-M3 below) scores FRE 74 / FK 6.6.

substantial.problem: 'The movement's own voice survives only in its enemies' papers' and 'the group's side was never put in writing that we hold' are unsupported, and the second is contradicted by the drafter's own source. Montero says Apolinario's letters about the Cofradía were read aloud at the Lucban meetings, and that his 'extensa correspondencia' was seized at Majayjay in September 1841. The group's side was put in writing; the Library just does not hold it. The quoted fact_table rows (Sancho's Relación title; Montero's political-aim sentence) do not carry either claim. Also, Montero's ground for a political aim is the exclusion of Spaniards and Chinese mestizos, not of Spaniards alone.
substantial.evidence: montero...t3, lines 1470-1472 ('se leían cartas de Apolinario referentes á la Cofradía por él instituida'); 1546-1547 ('ocupada la extensa correspondencia de Apolinario y su secretario', after the 19 September 1841 raid at line 1541); 2101 + 2132-2134 ('El no admitir en esta Cofradía españoles ni mestizos de sangley, y sí sólo indios puros, demuestra evidentemente que el objeto ... era político').
substantial.fix: Paragraph 4, first sentence: replace with "The movement speaks here only through its enemies." (rest of paragraph unchanged; scores FRE 67 / FK 6.9). Paragraph 5: replace whole with "Montero says the group let in no Spaniards and no Chinese mestizos. He takes that as proof of a political aim. That is his reading. Apolinario's letters were read aloud at the meetings, and were seized in 1841. The Library holds none of them. A modern study, by Reynaldo Ileto, starts its story of these movements in 1840. It is called Pasyon and Revolution (1979)." (FRE 65 / FK 6.3; the Ileto sentence rests on the book's subtitle, 'Popular Movements in the Philippines, 1840-1910', V-s). Fact_table rows: lines 1470-1472 and 1546-1547 as above; widen row 44 to lines 2131-2134 so 'españoles ni mestizos de sangley' is in the quote.

minor.problem: The year 1695 for the metropolitan's letter is Adoratskii's frame, not the letter's: the quoted letter carries no date (p. 50), and the year comes from his narration of Ignatii's sending of a priest and deacon 'in that year' (p. 49). The paragraph does not say so, and 'The details are his' sits two paragraphs later after the 1745-1808 sentences, where it reads as covering those only.

minor.problem: Adoratskii's thesis X is cut in a way that drops its counterweight: the same sentence goes on 'But even in this time it did not cease to hold to the basic principles of Orthodoxy and the tasks set for it.' Leaving it out makes his verdict sound wholly negative. 'a time of neglect and sorry state' and 'hard contact with China' are also unidiomatic.

AP7 HOLD UPHELD: Mackenzie prints no Catholic document of the period verbatim. The Pius IX rescript of 5 September 1861 is one clause (lines 2136-2138); Roccos's 1861 letter gives only its signature (6112-6114); the 1886 concordat, the 1887/1892 vicariates and the 1896 Syrian vicars apostolic (2020-2090) are Mackenzie's summary; the 1900 refusal of the Chaldean rite (4984-4985) is his statement, no text.
